facts.text: Automatic Emergency Braking (AEB), called an Advanced Emergency Braking System (AEBS) in United Nations vehicle regulations, is a function on modern cars and trucks that automatically brakes when a crash with a vehicle or person ahead is imminent.
facts.quote: Automatic Emergency Braking (AEB), called an Advanced Emergency Braking System (AEBS) in United Nations vehicle regulations, is the function on modern cars and trucks that brakes by itself when a crash with the vehicle or person ahead is about to happen.

facts.text: UN Regulation No. 152 for cars and vans requires a braking demand of at least 5.0 m/s², far above what heavy machines reach.
facts.quote: UN Regulation No. 152 for cars and vans requires a braking demand of at least 5.0 m/s², far above what heavy machines reach

facts.text: UN Regulation No. 131 covers heavy road vehicles.
facts.quote: UN Regulation No. 131 covers heavy road vehicles

facts.text: The US rule FMVSS 127 requires AEB on all new light vehicles by 1 September 2029.
facts.quote: the US rule FMVSS 127 requires AEB on all new light vehicles by 1 September 2029

facts.text: The US rule FMVSS 127 includes tests for unwanted braking.
facts.quote: the US rule FMVSS 127 requires AEB on all new light vehicles by 1 September 2029, with tests for unwanted braking

facts.text: Road AEB provides the booklet's richest source of measured effects, which are always marked as on-road evidence.
facts.quote: Road AEB is the booklet's richest source of measured effects, always marked as on-road evidence.

facts.text: On-road evidence shows that front warning plus AEB cut rear-end striking crashes by 50%.
facts.quote: Front warning plus AEB cut rear-end striking crashes by 50%

facts.text: On-road evidence shows that rear AEB cut backing crashes by 78%.
facts.quote: rear AEB cut backing crashes by 78%

facts.text: On-road evidence reports that AEB also raised the rate of being struck from behind by 20%.
facts.quote: but it also raised the rate of being struck from behind by 20%

facts.text: Road AEB assumes a hard, known surface, a vehicle that should stay away from everything, and speeds where time to collision works; heavy machines violate all three assumptions, limiting transfer of road AEB evidence.
facts.quote: road AEB assumes a hard, known surface, a vehicle that should stay away from everything, and speeds where time to collision works, and heavy machines break all three

facts.text: Regulators accepted virtual testing for car AEB only after years of correlation work, while retaining physical tests.
facts.quote: Regulators accepted virtual testing for car AEB only after years of correlation work, with physical tests retained

facts.text: Road AEB is the closest precedent for both the heavy off-road braking function and simulation as evidence; the booklet uses road AEB methods but refuses to copy its numerical results.
facts.quote: Road AEB is the closest precedent for both the function and the use of simulation as evidence, so the booklet mines it for methods while refusing to copy its numbers
